text:
Lena: Heads up — I'm WFH on the balcony today and the local sparrows think I'm throwing a live concert. Anyone got recs for an inexpensive wireless lav or handheld that survives ambient birdsong? Pic: <https://files.slack.com/files-pri/T12345-FBIRD/balcony_bird.jpg>

Marco: :bird: :laughing: Rode Wireless GO II is great for quick mobile setups. Also try `Suppress background noise: High` in Zoom if you can't mic up.

Priya: Second Rode if budget allows. For < $100, try a wired lav tied into your phone with a TRRS adapter — less latency and fewer pairing issues.

Tom: +1 on wired if you're near your laptop. If you want pocket wireless, Sennheiser XSW-D1 was decent. Also consider a foam windscreen — birds are loud when they hit the mic.

Lena: Thanks! Anyone used the Rode Clips for shirts? Also, do noise-canceling headphones help for others on the call or just local listening?

Marco: Mics help the call attendees; headphones only help you hear. If the mic picks up birds it's out in the mix. For quick hacks, use `noise-suppression` in the app or run Krisp (or the built-in noise removal).

Priya: If you want to test, record a 10–15s clip and upload — easy to audition. (or let EchoBot capture a 10s sample?)

EchoBot: Captured 14s clip of `balcony_chirp_14s.wav` and uploaded to #random-files: <https://files.slack.com/files-pri/T12345-FCHIRP/balcony_chirp_14s.wav>

Tom: Listening — yep, high freq spikes around 2.5–5kHz. A simple HPF at 120Hz and notch 3–6k can reduce it, but that's getting into audio nerd territory :headphones:.

Lena: Awesome, thanks all. I ordered a cheap lav and a foam windscreen. Will report back with a victory or more bird memes. :seedling:

Marco: Please deliver bird memes. :party-parrot:

Priya: Quick poll — who had unexpected wildlife interrupt a call this week? React with :raised_hand: if yes.

Lena: @here also — if anyone needs a balcony office tour, I offer free tickets and chirp commentary. :microphone:
